newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends up, commercials sell late.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends up, commercials sell late.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended higher despite late commercial selling, traders said.

"Even though we ended higher, we really didn't follow Chicago and Kansas City at the close. We had late scale-up commercial selling and locals were buying it up, so it'll be interesting to see how we start off tomorrow," a trader said.

Spring wheat gained early on mill buying and spillover support from other U.S. wheat markets, which were buoyed by concerns over possible winterkill damage that could result from the bitter cold temperatures expected in the central U.S. Plains later this week.

Although they were late sellers, commercials had been solid buyers at the midsession. One trader said commercials were bidding as much as 12-1/2 cents for the March/May spread at midsession. It closed Monday at 11 cents.
MGE spring wheat closed two to 6-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with March up 6-1/4 cents at $3.90-1/4, its highest closing price since December 20.
LFG sold one million March bushels, most of it late. Country Hedging sold 600,000 March, and Wilson bull-spread 400,000 March/May.
MGE barley closed steady to four cents per cwt higher, with March up four cents at $6.69.
